tool.name: SuperDecisions (web, V4 Platform)
tool.version: v0.5.14 (as displayed on the application's login page)

captured.notes: Model building and judgment entry were automated in the operator's browser (operator signed in and supervised); both completed judgment matrices were read from screen and checked against the fixture entry-by-entry before the results were transcribed verbatim (see the transcript artifact). The operator manually checked the session and outputs before this capture was committed.

criteria.notes: 'Normal' column of the Priorities panel; the 'Inconsistency' figure 0.0206 is transcribed as cr; lambda_max and CI are not displayed. The tool's 0.218 for Academics independently corroborates the fixture's reading that the source paper's printed 0.213 is a last-digit slip for 0.218.

location.notes: 'Normal' column of the Priorities panel; the 'Inconsistency' figure 0.0923 is transcribed as cr. The tool's 0.284 for U. Michigan matches the exact eigenvector value 0.2841 where the source paper prints 0.283 (sum-to-1.000 rounding).

ri_table.name: other
ri_table.source: Determined numerically across the four SuperDecisions web captures in this repository (matrices spanning n = 2..7): the displayed inconsistencies imply effective RI(3) = 0.52, RI(4) = 0.89, RI(5) = 1.12, RI(6) = 1.25 and RI(7) = 1.35 at the displayed four-decimal precision (CI values recomputed from the fixtures' matrices). All but RI(5) coincide with the random-index estimates printed in T. L. Saaty, Theory and Applications of the Analytic Network Process, 2005, p. 31 (0.52, 0.89, 1.11, 1.25, 1.35); RI(5) = 1.12 coincides with the Saaty (1980) table instead. No single published table matches all observations, and vendor documentation or source stating the table was not located.

prioritization_method: principal-eigenvector (inferred: all displayed priorities equal the fixture's principal-eigenvector expected values at display precision, including entries where the column-normalization alternates differ)

matrices.criteria.priorities.note: All four displayed priorities equal the fixture's derived expected values at the tool's display precision.

matrices.criteria.cr.note: Displayed 0.0206 vs the fixture's published CR 0.02 (difference 0.0006, outside the fixture's tolerance). See the capture-level explanation: this is a random-index difference, not a priorities or CI difference.

matrices.location.priorities.note: All five displayed priorities equal the fixture's derived expected values at the tool's display precision.

matrices.location.cr.note: Displayed 0.0923 vs the fixture's published CR 0.092 (difference 0.0003, within tolerance). The tool's observed effective RI(5) = 1.12 coincides with the fixture's declared table at this matrix size, so no divergence arises here, unlike at n=4.

explanation: The criteria matrix's displayed inconsistency (0.0206) differs from the fixture's published CR (0.02) because the tool computes its inconsistency with a different random-index value at n=4 (effective RI 0.89, consistent with the estimates in Saaty's 2005 ANP book) than the Saaty (1980) table the fixture declares (RI 0.90). The consistency index itself agrees: CI = 0.0183 from the fixture's matrix, which gives 0.0204 under the fixture's table - the published value 0.02 within its tolerance - and 0.0206 under the tool's. All priorities match the expected values at the tool's display precision. This is a documented random-index difference, not a disagreement about the judgments or the eigenvector.

reverify.instructions: Sign in at superdecisions.com. Create a model with clusters 'Goal' (node: Choose best college), 'Criteria' (nodes: Location, Ambience, Reputation, Academics) and 'Colleges' (nodes: Swarthmore, Northwestern, U. Michigan, Vanderbilt, CMU). Connect the goal node to the Criteria cluster and the Location node to the Colleges cluster. In Assess/Compare > Matrix view enter the fixture's two matrices (a value in cell (row, column) means the row element is that many times more preferred; enter each judgment as a value >= 1 in the dominant element's row and reciprocals fill automatically); the full matrices as entered are in the transcript artifact. Read the Priorities panel and 'Inconsistency' figure for each reference node (Choose best college, then Location). The model file ahp-fixture-college-rwsaaty-1987.sdm4 is saved in the operator's Google Drive and can be exported on request.
